page: Microsoft Azure M32ls is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical Intel Xeon 8280L cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing two threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz and is equipped with a 105 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. Memory capacity is 256.0 GB, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. The instance includes 1049 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance divergence between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is weak, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% categories respectively. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also register in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, consistently achieve average tier results. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks fall within the middle 50% range, as do Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations, which reached 20.68 million operations per second.

Given the 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, this server represents a memory-optimized configuration within its hardware class, offering a high memory density relative to compute resources. It is suited for workloads that can leverage parallel processing to bypass single-core performance limitations, such as multi-threaded database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and moderate-scale LLM inference. For instance, prompt processing for a 7B parameter model achieves 37.67 tokens per second, whereas larger 70B models drop to a poor 3.64 tokens per second. The server provides a balanced resource-to-cost profile for memory-intensive applications that do not require GPU acceleration or high single-threaded clock speeds.
